prompt.brief: Design an experimentation platform that assigns users consistently to variants, captures exposure and outcome events, detects sample-ratio or data-quality issues, and produces decision-ready analyses.
successSignals: Define experiment lifecycle, targeting, mutual exclusion, allocation, deterministic assignment, exposure logging, metrics, guardrails, and stopping rules.
Keep assignment fast and stable across retries/devices where intended; support ramping, holdouts, overrides, and emergency kill switches.
Separate flag evaluation from event collection and statistical analysis; make experiment definitions and analysis snapshots versioned.
Explain interference, novelty, missing exposure, sample-ratio mismatch, privacy, sequential peeking, auditability, and degraded evaluation.

functional: Create experiments, define populations/variants/metrics, assign subjects, evaluate flags, record exposures/outcomes, and analyze results.
Support gradual rollout, holdout groups, mutually exclusive layers, audience exclusions, guardrail alerts, approvals, and experiment history.
Make assignments deterministic and auditable, handle identity changes, replay events, correct metrics, and stop unsafe variants immediately.
nonFunctional: Return a stable assignment with p95 evaluation under 20ms and publish trusted analyses only after exposure/data-quality checks.
Scale to 1,000 concurrent experiments and 100M subjects without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100M subjects, 1,000 experiments, and 10M exposure events per minute
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Experimentation platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Experimentation platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Experimentation platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Experimentation platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Experimentation platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Experimentation platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Experimentation platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Experimentation platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Experimentation platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
